case_title: Kailas & Ors. v. State of Maharashtra Tr. Taluka P.S.
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under various provisions of the IPC and sentenced to RI for six months with fine; sentenced to RI for one year with fine for the offence punishable under Sections 354/34 IPC; sentenced under Section 323/34 IPC to three months RI with a fine; convicted and sentenced under Section 3 of the SC/ST Act
high_court_outcome: Acquitting the accused for the offence u/s. 3 of the SC/ST Act, however, upholding conviction under the provisions of the /PC; directing each accused to pay fine of Rs. 5000/- to the victim
offence_finally_established: Culpable homicide, cruelty, and violation of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act
neutral_facts: The accused persons beat a young woman, who was a member of a Scheduled Tribe, with fists and kicks, stripped her naked after tearing her clothes, and then paraded her in naked condition on the road of a village while beating and abusing her. The victim was accompanied by police during the panchanama, where she showed the area from her house to the place in front of a shop. The police seized her torn clothes. A medical certificate confirmed two contusions on the victim's body. The accused were convicted under various sections of the IPC and the SC/ST Act, but the High Court acquitted them for the offence under the SC/ST Act and upheld the conviction under the IPC, directing them to pay a fine to the victim.
